assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showed that membraneless compartments such as P granules and nucleoli behave as liquid-like condensates formed by phase separation, giving cell organisation a general thermodynamic description in terms of multivalency, phase behaviour and interfaces. It is a new concept of molecular organisation with broad reach across cell biology, disease (including aggregation) and biomolecular design, and it sits squarely in physical chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne established the liquid-droplet picture in cells (P granules, 2009 onward). Rosen's multivalent-interaction work gave the quantitative in vitro framework. Pappu and Mittag contributed sequence-encoded physics of disordered regions, so excluding them is a real choice, but three names support a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: About fifteen years of work with wide uptake. Confirmation is strong for the general idea, but the functional relevance of phase separation in vivo, as against mere demixing in vitro, is still actively debated, so timing is somewhat early.
uncertainties: Debate over physiological versus artefactual condensates
Whether the credit fairly covers theory (Pappu, Mittag) as well as cell experiments
Whether the Chemistry committee would treat this as chemistry rather than cell biology

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a lipid self-assembly and pKa-controlled interfacial design problem that made mRNA and siRNA medicines possible, with enormous demonstrated impact (siRNA therapy, COVID-19 vaccines). The discovery rests on lipid phase behaviour, membrane fusion propensity and charge regulation, which are close to my own field.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues developed the ionizable lipid and the controlled-mixing formulation. Anderson and Langer developed combinatorial lipidoid libraries, and MacLachlan, Hope and Madden were central to the early siRNA-LNP work. The credit is distributed and contestable, and the 2023 Medicine prize to Karikó and Weissman covered the nucleoside modification, not the delivery vehicle.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at very large scale, and the principles have been reproduced independently by many groups. Recognition is timely given the impact.
uncertainties: Credit among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is hard to resolve
Possible overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize
Whether the molecular discovery is distinct from the formulation engineering

assessment.nobel_worthiness: PROTACs and molecular glue degraders opened a new modality of induced proximity that removes proteins instead of inhibiting them, with a clear chemical concept, wide uptake in drug discovery and clinical candidates reaching late stages. The concept is original and generalisable.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched the PROTAC concept (2001) and Crews led the development of small-molecule PROTACs. Ciulli contributed the structural and mechanistic basis for VHL-based degraders. Handa and Ito's thalidomide-cereblon work is the key molecular-glue link and arguably could belong to the prize. Credit is genuinely open.
assessment.maturity: Strong mechanistic confirmation and many clinical programmes, but no approved PROTAC yet as far as I know, so the lasting impact is not yet fully shown.
uncertainties: Whether approval of a degrader drug is needed before recognition
How to split the credit between PROTACs and the cereblon molecular glue mechanism
I cannot check clinical status independently

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape theory and the funnel concept explain how proteins fold to unique structures despite a huge conformational space, using statistical mechanics and thermodynamics in the way I value. It is a unifying physical-chemical principle that shaped how folding, misfolding and aggregation are understood.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes, Onuchic and Bryngelson formulated the funnel and the minimal-frustration principle. Dill contributed lattice and hydrophobic-collapse models, and Fersht the experimental mapping through phi-value analysis. Choosing three leaves out either theory or experiment, which is the central allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Theory is long established and independently supported by simulation and experiment. The protein structure prediction prize in 2024 may reduce the sense of urgency but does not remove the claim.
uncertainties: Overlap in public perception with the 2024 Chemistry prize on protein structure
Whether to include experimental mapping by Fersht
Several theorists have partially overlapping claims

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The dye-sensitized mesoporous TiO2 solar cell introduced a molecular, interfacial approach to photovoltaics with a high-surface-area nanocrystalline electrode, linking electron-transfer kinetics, colloids and surface chemistry. It had very wide influence on photoelectrochemistry and later led to perovskite cells.
assessment.attribution: Grätzel is the central figure, with O'Regan and Grätzel's 1991 Nature paper as the core. Hagfeldt is a later contributor in mechanism and optimisation, so the proposed set is a judgement call and a one- or two-person prize could be defensible.
assessment.maturity: More than thirty years of work with extensive independent confirmation. Efficiency has been overtaken by other technologies, but the scientific contribution is established and recognition is arguably late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether Hagfeldt's contribution is at the level of a laureate
Commercial impact has been limited relative to the scientific influence
Perovskite solar cells could reframe the story

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry transferred intact non-covalent protein complexes, including membrane proteins and lipid-bound assemblies, into the gas phase, allowing stoichiometry, interactions and heterogeneity to be read directly. For someone studying lipid-protein interactions, the membrane protein and lipid binding applications are especially compelling.
assessment.attribution: Chait, Robinson and Heck each made decisive contributions in complexes, instrumentation and membrane protein analysis. Loo and Gross are also credited. Fundamental ionisation work was recognised in the 2002 prize, so the contribution here is the application to intact complexes.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and widely used in structural biology. Some open questions about how well gas-phase structures reflect solution structure remain, but the technique is mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 mass spectrometry prize
Whether it is seen as a method rather than a concept
Fair allocation among five credited people

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors enable programmable single-nucleotide changes without double-strand breaks by combining deaminase chemistry with CRISPR targeting. This is an inventive piece of molecular chemistry with therapeutic consequences, and the first clinical results are encouraging.
assessment.attribution: Liu's laboratory made the decisive contribution, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead inventors of the cytosine and adenine base editors. Kondo and Nishida had an independent related approach. The proposed set reflects the original lab but ignores Kondo and Nishida.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly adopted and clinically relevant, but the 2020 Chemistry prize on CRISPR-Cas9 and the early clinical stage make this more likely premature, and Liu's other work is a competing candidate.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 prize
Early clinical evidence only
Whether to combine with prime editing (B041) or treat separately

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA origami turned DNA folding into a programmable route to nanoscale objects of arbitrary shape, an elegant case of molecular self-assembly governed by base-pairing thermodynamics. Applications range from nanoscale devices and sensors to biophysical tools.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund introduced the scaffolded origami method in 2006. Yin and Shih extended it to three dimensions and to functional systems, while Winfree and Yan contributed tile-based and 2D/3D assembly. Seeman, who pioneered DNA nanotechnology, is not in the credited list and has died, which complicates fair recognition.
assessment.maturity: Highly cited and independently replicated for two decades. Practical impact is still developing, and the field is arguably more of a toolbox than a single discovery, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Exclusion of Seeman from the credited list limits a fair attribution
Real-world applications still limited
Whether it should be recognised with other DNA nanotechnology contributions
